name: Industry life cycle
purpose: How do the forces change as the industry evolves?
apply: Place the industry with evidence (growth rates, exits, price wars)
Derive which forces will strengthen next

name: Strategic groups
purpose: With whom does the firm really compete?

parts.label: Definition
points: Rivalry is most intense within groups

parts.label: Uses
points: White spaces (opportunity) vs black holes (dead end)

apply: Pick two dimensions that really separate firms
Place the case firms, name the mobility barriers
Discuss empty spaces: white space or black hole?
example: Grocery retail: supermarkets · convenience stores · corner shops.

name: Blue Ocean & strategy canvas
purpose: How can a firm escape competition by creating new market space?

parts.label: Red vs blue ocean
points: Blue: new market space, competition minimized

parts.label: Strategy canvas
points: Adequate (above minimal level to survive) on contested CSFs
Invest in new CSFs valued but unexplored

parts.label: Value innovation
points: Leap in value for customers + lower costs

example: Nintendo: competing on technology failed (N64, GameCube, 3DS, Wii U); value innovation won (DS, Wii, Switch, Pokémon Go). Apple Vision Pro: new market claim → niche.

name: Four actions framework (ERRC)
purpose: How to redraw the value curve?

parts.label: Eliminate
points: Which factors the industry takes for granted should be eliminated?

parts.label: Raise
points: Which factors should be raised well above the industry standard?

parts.label: Reduce
points: Which factors should be reduced well below the industry standard?

parts.label: Create
points: Which factors should be created that the industry never offered?

apply: Fill all four boxes with concrete case features
Check: does it lower costs AND raise value? Does it attract noncustomers?
example: CitizenM: eliminate restaurants · reduce room size and reception · raise low-cost construction · create 5* location/bed with 3* price (“affordable luxury”).
